advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a divergence_report test with the current author writing under two+ foreign env ids, asserting the count and the joined id list.
evidence: tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py:33 defines a single `_OTHER_ENV`; all divergence tests (test_fsck_reports_env_id_divergence, test_a_shared_store_with_several_clones_is_not_reported) restamp events with only that one id
ABSENCE: no test constructs a `seen` set where the current author appears under two or more distinct foreign env ids
advisory.finding: divergence_report's multi-foreign-id rendering path is untested: every divergence/fsck test uses a single foreign env id (_OTHER_ENV), so the count phrase `{len(foreign)} other environment id(s)` and the `', '.join(foreign)` list are never exercised with more than one id. A regression producing a wrong count or mis-joined list of two+ orphaned ids would pass all current tests.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a store_event_env_ids test that passes low max_ids/max_files and asserts the scan stops at the cap.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:144 `if read >= max_files or len(found) >= max_ids: return found`
tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py:160-165 the only store_event_env_ids test exercises a single-id, single-file store
advisory.finding: The bounded discovery scan caps (_MAX_DISTINCT_IDS=4, _MAX_FILES_SCANNED=2000) and their early-return branches in store_event_env_ids have no test. A regression removing or breaking the cap (e.g. off-by-one, or dropping the `len(found) >= max_ids` guard) would go undetected — the only scan test (test_unreadable_events_do_not_crash_the_scan) uses one event and asserts a single-id result.
advisory.suggested_fix: Call store_event_env_ids(tracker, max_ids=1) / max_files=1 against a store with several distinct env ids and assert the returned set size honors the cap.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a scan that FAILED (OSError enumerating the store) from a genuinely empty store in `mint_env_id_guarded`, so an unreadable populated store is not silently treated as genesis.
evidence:
`try:
        entries = sorted(os.listdir(root))
    except OSError:
        return found` (returns empty set on an unreadable root) — src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:129-132

`prior = store_event_env_ids(root)` then `if not prior: return EnsureOutcome("env-id", "changed", f"generated {ENV_ID_FILE}")` — the genesis (silent) branch is taken whenever the scan yields nothing, including a scan that failed rather than a genuinely empty store — src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:220-223

Reachability: a re-clone whose ticket dirs are momentarily unreadable (permissions, races, partial checkout) reads as genesis and mints silently — the advisory warning is lost even though prior events exist. The attestation gate itself remains fail-closed, so impact is limited to the missing warning.
advisory.finding: `store_event_env_ids` swallows all OSErrors (on listing the tracker root, listing a ticket dir, or reading an event) and returns whatever partial set it has; when the root listing fails it returns an empty set. `mint_env_id_guarded` then observes `prior == set()` and takes the silent GENESIS branch — so an unreadable or permission-restricted populated store is silently re-identified with no re-identification warning, which is the exact silent-mint condition this change exists to prevent.
scenarios: A populated tracker with restricted directory permissions or a partial/racing checkout is re-cloned; the discovery scan fails to enumerate events and the new identity is minted with no warning.
